0.long_answer: Hereditary Partial Transcobalamin II Deficiency is an autosomal dominant metabolic syndrome characterized by the abnormal metabolism of methylcobalamin. Methylcobalamin plays a critical role in several biochemical pathways, including DNA synthesis and methylation processes. Defects in its metabolism can lead to disruptions in these pathways, resulting in neurological deficits such as intellectual disability (historically referred to as mental retardation), anemia, and various other neurological and developmental issues. Clinical studies and family pedigree analyses have identified this syndrome as autosomal dominant, differentiating it from other cobalamin metabolism disorders that may follow an autosomal recessive pattern.
